# Observed BigQuery answers recorded with tools/bqanswers. Unlike aggregate AVG's running
# mean, window AVG preserves infinities regardless of input order and tolerates a finite
# difference outside FLOAT64's range. The AVG documentation allows Infinity or NaN:
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/aggregate_functions.md
SELECT AVG(x) OVER () FROM UNNEST([CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64), CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64)]) AS x LIMIT 1
=> "-Infinity"

SELECT AVG(x) OVER () FROM UNNEST([CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64), CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64)]) AS x LIMIT 1
=> "NaN"

SELECT AVG(x) OVER () FROM UNNEST([CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64), 1.0]) AS x LIMIT 1
=> "Infinity"

SELECT AVG(x) OVER () FROM UNNEST([1.0, CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64)]) AS x LIMIT 1
=> "Infinity"

SELECT AVG(x) OVER () FROM UNNEST([CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64), CAST('nan' AS FLOAT64)]) AS x LIMIT 1
=> "NaN"

SELECT AVG(DISTINCT x) OVER () FROM UNNEST([CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64), CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64), NULL]) AS x LIMIT 1
=> "Infinity"

SELECT ARRAY(SELECT AVG(x) OVER (ORDER BY i ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM UNNEST([CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64), CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64), 1.0, 3.0]) AS x WITH OFFSET i ORDER BY i)
=> [{"v":"Infinity"},{"v":"Infinity"},{"v":"Infinity"},{"v":"2.0"}]

SELECT ARRAY(SELECT AVG(x) OVER (PARTITION BY p) FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS p, CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64) AS x), (1, CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64)), (2, 1.0), (2, 3.0)]) ORDER BY p, x)
=> [{"v":"Infinity"},{"v":"Infinity"},{"v":"2.0"},{"v":"2.0"}]

SELECT AVG(x) OVER () FROM UNNEST([CAST('-1.7976931348623157e308' AS FLOAT64), CAST('1.7976931348623157e308' AS FLOAT64)]) AS x LIMIT 1
=> "0.0"

SELECT AVG(x) OVER () FROM UNNEST([0.1, 0.2, 0.3]) AS x LIMIT 1
=> "0.2"
